title: The APT Foundation Donates to an OzChild Carer In Need
author: Aaron
body:
We are brought together through generosity and community.

The APT Travel Group raised money for OzChild last Christmas, a donation which was matched by the APT Foundation. Rallied by the APT Travel Group staff member Patrice, a fantastic toy drive for Christmas was held in support of OzChild, the leading child welfare organisation, who are dedicated to improving the lives of at-risk children, young people and families in the community.

On receiving the donation, OzChild decided that the best way to use it was to support a kinship carer. In Pakenham, a carer looking after nine children was facing challenges every day. One of those challenges affected the day-to-day running of the home. The carer’s small, unreliable washing machine meant that in a household of 10, the carer’s small, unreliable washing machine simply couldn’t keep up with the ever-growing pile of laundry. The carer was struggling to get through a minimum of 20 loads every week.

Alison, the case worker supporting the carer, suggested the best way to spend this donation was by replacing this insufficient washing machine with a bigger and better model. The new 14.5kg washing machine was found at Harvey Norman Springvale in Victoria. Harvey Norman and the supplier kindly agreed to offer the appliance at below cost and the donation from the APT Foundation was used to purchase the washing machine.

“The carer was so excited about the washing machine!” says Alison. “She choked back tears as she told me how much easier it was going to be for her now.”

Alison shares that during her visit to the carer’s home, the carer’s excitement had spread to the children. They made sure to show Alison the new washing machine as soon as she stepped foot through the door.
 
“The carer said doing the washing for 10 people was taking her hours and hours every week, and she never felt like she was on top of it,” says Alison. “She asked to have her thanks passed onto everyone for this amazingly generous gift.”

Patrice was unable to operate the Easter raffle this year due to Covid-19 social distancing restrictions, so the APT Foundation made a further donation of $2,000 to OzChild in May 2020.
